cands.name: Dan Green
cands.bio: Republican nominee. Navy Reserve captain; Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Strategy and Force Development (2019-21, Trump administration); earlier Defense/State Department roles. Won the Aug 2026 GOP primary narrowly (about 25.4% to 24.4% over Ben Butler). Has not held elected office.
cands.local_ties: Residence not stated in sources found. New District 9 stretches from Orlando south to Lake Okeechobee: Osceola, Highlands, Indian River, Okeechobee, Glades counties plus parts of Orange and Polk (ClickOrlando; search summary).

record.text: Backed Gov. DeSantis over Trump in the 2024 presidential primary; now runs as a Trump Republican and served in Trump's first administration.
Positions: lower grocery prices via less regulation, balance the budget, deter China, voted yes on Amendment 3 (property tax), concerned about data centers.
Closing argument: says Soto has 'taken the district for granted'; cites a PhD in American politics and running a veterans coalition for DeSantis's re-election.

endorsements.text: Wikipedia's district page lists post-primary support from Trump, Gov. DeSantis, RNC Chair Joe Gruters and the NRCC; DeSantis rallied for him Sept 29, 2026 (search summary). Pre-primary he lacked a Trump endorsement.

cands.name: Darren Soto
cands.bio: Democrat, U.S. House since January 2017. Attorney; Florida House 2007-2012 and Florida Senate 2012-2016. Serves on Natural Resources and Energy and Commerce. Redistricting made his new District 9 more Republican-leaning (Cook PVI D+4 to R+8 per Wikipedia).
cands.local_ties: Central Florida (Orlando/Kissimmee area). New District 9 spans Orange/Osceola south to Lake Okeechobee.

record.text: Committees (119th): Natural Resources; Energy and Commerce. Caucuses include New Democrat Coalition, Hispanic Caucus (deputy chair), Problem Solvers.

Federal bills include the Shark and Billfish Protection Act (signed 2018), Pulse National Memorial designation, Puerto Rico Statehood Admission Act (2021), Kissimmee River wild-and-scenic study (enacted Dec 2022).
Closing argument cites secured federal funding including the I-4 expansion and Orlando airport Terminal C; on Amendment 3 he said 'Let the people decide'.

money_notes.text: Wikipedia: in 2022 he was named among eight House members dubbed the 'Blockchain Eight' who sought to curb SEC crypto investigations while receiving crypto-industry donations, including from groups linked to Sam Bankman-Fried.

endorsements.text: Per Wikipedia's district page: AFGE, Florida AFL-CIO, UAW, AIPAC, Democratic Majority for Israel, Latino Victory, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Sierra Club; post-primary also NEA, Florida Education Association, LCV and others.
